answers.answer: It came from the model's parametric memory, the knowledge left in the weights by pre-training, which the RAG paper describes as a parameterized implicit knowledge base used with no access to an external memory. The paper's list of downsides is that such a memory cannot easily be expanded or revised and that the model does not straightforwardly give insight into its predictions, with hallucination as the third item. There is no fact to open and edit, so the only correction is retraining.
accept: names the weights or parametric memory as the source
says the memory cannot easily be expanded or revised
says the model gives no straightforward insight into its predictions, so the fact cannot be inspected

answers.answer: The non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia, held outside the seq2seq transformer and reached through a pre-trained neural retriever. Given the input sequence used as a query, the retriever returns a top-K truncated distribution over text passages, so each of the K passages carries a probability rather than just a rank position.
accept: identifies it as a dense vector index of Wikipedia outside the model, reached by a neural retriever
says the retriever returns a top-K truncated distribution over passages
notes the passages carry probabilities, not just an ordered list

answers.answer: RAG-Sequence commits once: one retrieved document is a single latent variable used for the complete generated sequence, marginalised out under a top-K approximation. RAG-Token commits per token: a different latent document is drawn for each target token and marginalised accordingly. For sequence classification, where the target class is a target sequence of length one, the two are equivalent, because there is only one token for the per-token draw to vary over.
accept: RAG-Sequence uses one document for the whole output sequence
RAG-Token draws a different document per generated token
the two are equivalent for classification or a length-one target sequence

answers.answer: RAG-Token. Because a different latent document is drawn for each target token and marginalised accordingly, the generator can take content from several documents while producing one answer. RAG-Sequence uses the same document for the complete sequence, so mixing content across documents within one answer is not available to it.
accept: answers RAG-Token
because a different document is drawn per token and marginalised, letting the generator combine content from several documents
contrasts with RAG-Sequence being locked to one document for the whole sequence

answers.answer: The retriever and generator are trained jointly, with no direct supervision on which document should be retrieved. The retriever's distribution over passages supplies the weights in the marginalisation that produces the sequence probability p(y|x), so raising the probability of a passage that helps the generator reach the target output raises the likelihood of that output. The retrieval signal comes through the generator's likelihood rather than from any label naming a correct passage.
accept: says the two are trained jointly with no direct supervision on which document to retrieve
says the retriever's passage probabilities weight the marginalisation that gives p(y|x)
explains that the learning signal reaches the retriever through the likelihood of the target output

answers.answer: An extractive system answers by selecting a span out of a retrieved document, so if the answer string is in none of the retrieved documents there is no span to select and its ceiling in those cases is zero. RAG generates the answer instead, drawing on the parametric memory as well as the retrieved passages, which is how it reached 11.8% accuracy on Natural Questions in exactly those cases.
accept: says an extractive reader can only copy a span from the retrieved text
concludes that with the answer absent from every retrieved document there is nothing to extract, so the score is structurally zero
says RAG generates rather than extracts and can use knowledge in the weights as well

answers.answer: Providing provenance for a model's decisions and updating its world knowledge. A closed-book answer is produced with no retrieval, conditioned only on the parameters, and the paper lists the inability to give straightforward insight into predictions as a downside of that setup, so there is nothing to point at as the answer's source. The same setup makes updating hard because a parametric model cannot easily expand or revise its memory, whereas a retrieval-conditioned answer comes from documents selected and passed in as context, held in an index outside the weights.
accept: names provenance for decisions and updating world knowledge as the two open problems
says a closed-book answer uses no retrieval and is conditioned only on the parameters, leaving no identifiable source to cite
says a parametric model cannot easily expand or revise its memory, while the retrieved documents and the index sit outside the weights
